# Custom Operating Systems
The operating system a computer boots, Gridline OS, is a Wire program like any other. You can read it, change it, and boot your own version.
## Booting your own - [mono]new myos os[/mono] copies the OS's source into [mono]myos.wire[/mono]. - Change it: rename the prompt, add commands, or start from scratch. - [mono]build myos.wire boot.bin[/mono] builds it as [mono]boot.bin[/mono]. - [mono]reboot[/mono] restarts the computer, which boots [mono]boot.bin[/mono] from its disk instead of the OS it came with.
## When it goes wrong If [mono]boot.bin[/mono] won't load, or it crashes or ends, the computer starts the OS it came with instead, and keeps doing so until it is rebooted or loses power. A broken OS can't lock anyone out. [mono]rm boot.bin[/mono] and then [mono]reboot[/mono] puts things back.
## Other programs that come with it The text editor, nano, is a Wire program too: [mono]new mynano nano[/mono] copies its source to change and build as your own.
[mono]man boot[/mono] on any computer explains it all again.
